mappings.note: Measure several objects with a metre scale and tabulate the results. LO-46 is 'measure physical quantities and express them in SI units, for example length' verbatim; LO-43 covers recording the observations.
Sort things around you into moving and at rest AND justify each call. LO-42 for the classification, LO-43 because the justification is an observation the student must record and defend.
Does the falling orange, the march-past, the pushed box move in a straight line? Recognising rectilinear motion, which LO-42 names among its own classification examples.
How visually challenged students measure using raised tactile markings. An adaptation of measurement to a real need, LO-49; no measuring is done by the candidate, so not LO-46.
The whirled eraser and the merry-go-round as circular motion. Circular motion is one of LO-42's three named categories.
Pull the hanging eraser aside and release: to-and-fro, like a swing. Identifying oscillatory motion, the periodic category of LO-42.
The pressed metal strip vibrating up and down is also oscillatory. Placing a less obvious case in the same LO-42 category.
Classify observed motions as linear, circular or oscillatory with a justification each. LO-42's 'motion as rectilinear, circular and periodic' exactly.
Match each length -- city distance, coin thickness, eraser, school ground -- to km, mm, cm or m. Choosing the right SI unit for a quantity, LO-46.
True/false covering linear motion, the definition of motion and the km-to-cm conversion. LO-42 for the motion statements, LO-46 for the unit relation the third statement tests.
Handspan is not a standard unit. Tests what qualifies as an SI-derived unit of length, LO-46.
Survey the scales and tapes at home and school and record the least count of each. LO-43 for the survey and its tabulated record, LO-46 for the measuring-instrument resolution it establishes.
Deepa's mother asks for char angula more length. A traditional unit used in a real transaction, LO-49; the item tests the everyday practice, not the measurement itself.
Why the friends got different handspan readings for one table. The item asks for the CAUSE of the discrepancy, LO-44, not for a measurement.
The SI unit of length is the metre. LO-46's own content.
One metre is 100 centimetres. An SI unit relation, LO-46.
Why metres are awkward for city distances and page thicknesses. Choosing a unit of appropriate size, LO-46.
The least count of a 15-cm classroom scale is 1 mm. The resolution of a measuring instrument, LO-46.
Ten millimetres in a centimetre. An SI unit relation, LO-46.
List three objects each best expressed in mm, cm and m. Matching quantity to unit, LO-46.
Name the motion type on each portion of a roller-coaster track. Sorting a single journey into LO-42's motion categories.
Which of plywood, paper, cloth, rubber and steel Tasman should NOT use for a metre scale. The answer turns on stretchability and tearing -- a differentiation of materials by their properties, LO-41.
Express 1.5 km in metres. A unit conversion within SI, LO-46.
Measure the curved base of a tumbler. Measuring a length that a rigid scale cannot take directly, LO-46.
Measure a friend's height and express it in metres, centimetres and millimetres. One measurement in three SI units, LO-46.
Estimate how many coins span the notebook's side, then VERIFY with a 15-cm scale. LO-46 for the measurement and LO-43 because estimate-then-check is the investigative move the item marks.
Two examples each of linear, circular and oscillatory motion. LO-42's three named categories.
Why standard units beat handspans and angula -- consistency between people. The rationale for SI, LO-46.
A flexible tape for tree girth or chest size. Selecting the right instrument for a real job, LO-49; the item is about tool choice rather than reading a value.
Place the scale in contact with the object, along its length. Correct measuring technique, LO-46.
A broken-zero scale: 11.5 cm minus 2.0 cm gives 9.5 cm. A measurement actually computed, LO-46.
What a reference point is. The concept that makes position and motion describable -- explaining the phenomenon, LO-45, rather than sorting motions, which is LO-42.
Why the friends disagreed about which was nearer -- each used their own house as reference. The item asks for the cause of the disagreement, LO-44.
Identify Delhi as the reference point for the kilometre stones. Applying the reference-point idea to read a real situation, LO-45.
When an object is in motion -- when its position changes with respect to a reference point over time. The definition of the phenomenon, LO-45.
Seated passengers are at rest relative to Deepa on the same bus. Explaining relativity of motion, LO-45.
Motion along a straight line is linear. LO-42's rectilinear category.
A merry-go-round is circular motion. LO-42's circular category.
Definition of oscillatory motion as to-and-fro about a fixed position. Defining an LO-42 category.
A child on a swing is oscillatory. Placing an instance in an LO-42 category.
Periodic motion repeats after a fixed time interval. LO-42 names periodic motion as one of its three categories.
Fathom is not from ancient Indian measure, unlike angula, dhanusa and yojana. Historical units of length, LO-46.
Assertion-reason: handspan readings vary BECAUSE there is no fixed standard. The reason clause is the cause of the variation, LO-44.

Which statements hold -- the SI unit, eye directly above the mark, flexible tape for curves. All three are measuring practice, LO-46. The stem retains only one of the three numbered statements its options reference.
A carpenter's marked metal rod as a measuring scale in standard units. Applying measurement to a trade, LO-49.
The international system is SI, the modern metric system. LO-46's own content.
How to measure with a broken zero mark -- start from a full mark and subtract. Measuring technique, LO-46.
Motion along a circular path is circular motion. LO-42's circular category.
Angula is the width of a finger. A historical unit of length defined, LO-46.
How linear motion DIFFERS from circular motion. The verb is 'differ', and the basis is the path's structure, so LO-41 rather than the sorting outcome LO-42.
Which is NOT one of the motion types the section covers. Tests the boundary of LO-42's category set.
Clock hands trace circular motion. Placing an instance in an LO-42 category.
Assertion-reason: an object can be at rest for one reference point and moving for another because motion is relative. Explaining the phenomenon, LO-45.
Which listed motions are oscillatory -- the swing and the plucked string, not the car. An LO-42 sorting. The stem preserves only the last of the three numbered items.
Why a 15-cm scale is inefficient for a classroom -- repeated laying accumulates error. Judging instrument fitness and measurement error, LO-46.
One inch is about 2.54 cm. A conversion between a non-SI and an SI unit, LO-46.
Circular motion that is also periodic means each revolution takes the same time. Combines two of LO-42's categories.
The engine piston as reciprocating, both linear and oscillatory. A borderline case placed against LO-42's categories.
Deepa's mother asked for a two-metre cloth piece. A measurement used in an everyday purchase, LO-49; the item is narrative recall rather than a measuring task.
Name a body part traditionally used to measure length. Non-standard units of length, LO-46.
